_evidence: The nine 0x38-byte render-state records at 0x7ad638 + k*0x38 (k 0..8): 0x531803 returns ebx = 0x7ad638 when the selector's bit in [0x7ad848] is set, else 0x7ad670 + i*0x38 with the selector i = [0x7ad87c] in 0..7 (sel_00531859), so 0x7ad638 is simply record -1 of the same array and selector 7 is 0x7ad7f8, the 'current' copy destination of 0x5303f7. All 504 bytes are varied (u8 background), then the fields the users test get value lists hitting both outcomes: 0x53026a 'and eax,0x1867f83c; cmp' on dword +0 (0x1867f83c/0x99e7ff3c/0xffffffff/0x1867f83d match, 0/0xe79807c3/0x1867f838 miss) and 'and eax,0x16; cmp' on dword +4 (0x16/0x17/0x1f match, 0x06/0/0xffffffe9/0x12 miss); 0x5303f7 'test [ebx+0x10],0x99e7ff3c' (0/1/0x661800c3 clear, 0x99e7ff3c/4/0x80000000/0x1867f83c set; 0x530162 tests the same dword with 0x1867f83c) and 'cmp byte [esi+0x1d],0xff'; 0x530162 'cmp byte [ebx+0x24|0x25],0'. Every byte pattern is valid: plain and/or/test/compares and a 0x38-byte copy; the copied dword +0x18 lands in 0x7ad810, the divisor of 0x4126e2 (via 0x530012), which maps 0 to 1 and divides (0x10000 + d/2) unsigned, so no value faults.
